prompt:
Extract a SysML v2 model from the document as a list of facts. Each fact has unit_id (the sentence it comes from), type and slots. Give only the slots that have a value, as a list of {slot, value} pairs; for composition give one 'parts' pair per part.

Types and slots:
  attribute(owner,name,value,unit) action(performer,label) state(owner,label) constraint(subject,expression) requirement(subject,text)
  composition(whole,parts) flow(source,target,payload) succession(before,after) transition(from,to,trigger) allocation(action,to)

Name each element by its full name as first introduced in the document.
RULES:
- Resolve every entity-valued slot using all the text you are given. If a sentence refers to an element by an alias, abbreviation, pronoun or shorter description, write the element's full name as first introduced. If a sentence says an element receives or uses an item and the text you are given states which element produces or sends that item, emit a flow from that producer to the receiver. If an element cannot be determined from the text you are given, use null; never guess.
- Never write placeholder words such as "any", "all", "some state" for an unstated element; use null.
- Do not merge differently named things unless the text says they are the same.
- Emit one action for EVERY behavior verb phrase, including passive voice (performer null), capability statements, displays, logs, generates and reports. label = the verbatim verb phrase with its object.
- Emit a requirement for every NORMATIVE statement (shall, must, should, will, is required to, needs to). Purpose, goal or benefit sentences are not requirements.
- Emit a state for every named mode or state; transitions use the state names, with from null when the prior state is not stated.
- Emit a succession only for an EXPLICIT temporal connective between two actions ("then", "after", "once", "before", "when ... is complete", "next", "finally"); before/after are the action labels. Never use succession for cause or data transfer.
- Resolve a pronoun or "this/these" performer to the element named in the preceding sentence and write that element's name; if it cannot be resolved, use null. Never output a pronoun as a slot value.
- Drop determiners and quantifiers from element names ("Each Soil Moisture Probe" -> "Soil Moisture Probe", "the system" -> "system").
- allocation.to must be a component or actor, never a mode or state.
- Emit a constraint for every threshold, limit, period or deadline stated with a number; expression = the verbatim phrase.
- Emit a flow for every sentence in which an element sends, transmits, reports, displays, commands or delivers an item (target null if the receiver is not named).
 Also list under "entities" every system element, actor or item named in the document units, with its full name and any alias the text explicitly declares for it (e.g. 'hereafter X', 'known as X', 'called X'); aliases [] if none. Return JSON {"entities": [...], "facts": [...]}.

Offshore wind O&M; scope Grid Interface Relay (Wildmere); excludes public grid, non-farm port ops. Wildmere: Export Limit Advisory→Grid Dispatcher when capability<target; applies accepted ceiling, records time; keeps protection settings unless authorized switching plan. Turbine Controller (Glassfin): validated commands within protections, blocks conflicts, safe mode on auxiliary loss; Pitch Deviation Notice. Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor→Turbine Sensor Bus. Offshore Substation (Morrowick): Main Transformer, export cable, Export Cable Monitor, station service transformers, Fire Detection Panel; Transformer Tap Snapshot→Shore Control Room; mode Substation Degraded. Substation Operator: switching after state check plus Control Engineer authorization; notifies Grid Dispatcher. Emergency Generator (Foxglove): auto-start on auxiliary loss, no unapproved paralleling; Start Test Trace. Shore Control Room keeps last validated limit on comms loss; Switching Window Acknowledgment. Grid Dispatcher priority safety>protection>export. Fleet Dispatch Console (Sable Orchard): Position Quality Flag. Mode Grid Constraint: Duty Planner records basis/authorization/handover; Control Engineer reduces stepwise, restores gradually after authorization. Maintenance Planning Engine (Thistle Crown): Squall Window Bulletin, Deferred Task Rationale. Weather Service→Weather Analyst (Wave Burst Record, Visibility Confidence Note)→Duty Planner. Duty Planner: mobilization (CTV/Daughter Craft/SOV/Helideck), Transfer Manifest Addendum→Vessel Master; restoration after Field Supervisor clear. CTV: Harness Audit Card. SOV: Recovery Basket Load Sheet. Personnel reconciliation: Marine Coordinator sets expected count; separate counts per vessel/location; Vessel Master verifies aboard before departure; North/South Access Scanner record access; Personnel Tracking Console count correction→verified personnel total (reason recorded). Discrepancy: Marine Coordinator pauses transfers, informs Shore Control Room, escalates to Duty Planner; Vessel Master safe position; resume only after Marine Coordinator confirms reconciliation/authorized response; included in shift handover. Software lifecycle: each component has owner, approved version, baseline (versions, parameters, dependencies, hardware revisions); access-controlled repos; changes off live; releases from approved source; SCADA Engineer verifies image via Firmware Hash Attestation before loading; Control Engineer confirms purpose/scope; technical approval before scheduling; extra scrutiny for protection/control; representative

Document units:
S611: Operational handover records identify the deployed change, any outstanding limitations, and the responsible technical contact.
S612: Emergency arrangements define who may direct an incident, who supports rescue, and who may authorize a return to work.
S613: The Shore Control Room maintains the incident log and provides a single operational point of contact for offshore teams.
S614: The Rescue Coordinator leads rescue planning and coordinates requests for external assistance.
S615: The Field Supervisor directs personnel at the affected work site until control is formally transferred.
S616: The Vessel Master retains authority over vessel safety, navigation, and decisions to approach or withdraw from a casualty.
S617: The HSE Officer advises on personnel hazards, rescue procedures, and the use of emergency equipment.
S618: The Marine Coordinator maintains awareness of vessel locations, access constraints, and available marine support.
S619: The Personnel Tracking Console supports personnel accounting, but the incident lead verifies headcounts with the teams involved.
S620: Crew Transfer Vessel operations are suspended when sea conditions, visibility, or transfer arrangements exceed approved limits.
S621: A Daughter Craft may support a local response only when its crew, equipment, and launch conditions are suitable.
S622: A Service Operations Vessel may provide accommodation, medical support, and a stable platform when its position and capability permit.
S623: The Helideck is used for evacuation only when aviation conditions, deck readiness, and receiving arrangements are acceptable.
S624: The Weather Service provides forecast information for planning, while operational decisions account for observed local conditions.
S625: The Metocean Buoy provides site measurements that help assess whether a planned response remains feasible.
S626: The Weather Analyst interprets forecast uncertainty and communicates material changes to the Rescue Coordinator.
S627: The Operations Radio Console supports communications between the Shore Control Room, vessels, and offshore work teams.
S628: Emergency Generator readiness is checked as part of site emergency preparedness and restoration planning.
S629: The Fire Detection Panel provides alarm indications that responders use alongside direct reports from personnel on site.
S630: The Control Engineer supports remote shutdown actions when communications and equipment status allow safe intervention.
S631: Electrical recovery work requires qualified personnel, verified isolation, and a safe means of access before hands-on activity begins.
S632: Recovery of injured or incapacitated personnel may be delayed by vessel motion, limited access, lifting capacity, or deteriorating conditions.
S633: Offshore recovery plans identify the point at which continued response would expose rescuers to unacceptable risk.
